entries.title: Boundary matching for optimized block passage costs
entries.statement: Draft audit concept; independent review pending. In unrestricted iid FPP on Z^2 with edge weights uniform on {1,2}, T((0,0),(1,1))=min(A1+B1,A2+B2), where A1=w((0,0),(1,0)), A2=w((0,0),(0,1)), B1=w((1,0),(1,1)) and B2=w((0,1),(1,1)). For L=min(A1,A2)+min(B1,B2), P(T>L)=1/8, E(T-L)=1/8, Var(T)=23/64, Var(L)=3/8 and Cov(L,T-L)=-1/16. Independence of the two edge collections does not justify scalar block composition or independence of the matching penalty.
assumptions: Nearest-neighbor undirected FPP on the full Z^2 lattice

entries.title: Single-edge forcing and tied minimizing paths
entries.statement: Draft audit concept; independent review pending. For nearest-neighbor FPP on Z^d with every edge weight in {1,2}, let T_e(1) and T_e(2) be the passage times between fixed distinct vertices after forcing edge e to weight 1 or 2, with all other weights held fixed. Then T_e(2)-T_e(1)=1 if and only if every minimizing path in the forced-low environment uses e; otherwise the difference is zero. Membership in one arbitrarily selected geodesic is insufficient.
assumptions: All weights take integer values 1 or 2
All other edge weights held fixed under the two forcings
A minimizing path means any path attaining passage time, not a selected tie representative

entries.title: Variance transfer through a centered matching error
entries.statement: Draft audit concept; independent review pending. For square-integrable T_n=L_n+G_n, if ||G_n-EG_n||_2=o(n^(1/3)) and c*n^(2/3)<=Var(L_n)<=C*n^(2/3) for fixed 0<c<=C and all sufficiently large n, then Var(T_n)/Var(L_n)->1; in particular log Var(T_n)/(2 log n)->1/3.
assumptions: Square-integrable real random variables T_n,L_n,G_n on a common probability space for each n

relations.rationale: The finite counterexample exhibits an endpoint-matching penalty; the conditional L2 statement specifies sufficient centered-error control to transfer a variance exponent in a sequence of such decompositions.

The same positive integer-weight square has tied optimal routes, so preserving the common boundary endpoint and distinguishing all minimizers from a selected minimizer are both necessary audit checks on optimized passage costs.
The explicit failure of scalar block composition obstructs a candidate method for controlling point-to-point variance exponents; it does not refute the exponent conjecture.
